title: Isolation of rodent eyes for analysis of diabetic retinopathy
author: Timothy Kern
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8fjhtkn

steps.title: Anesthetize the animal
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal using any suitable anesthetic.

steps.title: Isolate the eyes
steps.instruction: Carefully remove both eyes from the socket without compressing or pushing on the eye or skull.

substeps.instruction: Place thumb and pointer finger on either side of the eye and spread them to stretch the skin around the eye.
Using fine, sharp scissors, make 3-5 deep (5-10mm) cuts by forcing the scissors into the eye socket.
Push the scissors back into the eye socket to cut the optic nerve, ensuring some optic nerve remains attached to the eye.

steps.title: Fix the tissue
steps.instruction: Immediately place both eyes into 10% buffered formalin (pH 7.4) in a microfuge tube.

substeps.instruction: Ensure tissue is collected fresh within 10-15 min of death (tissue post-mortem more than 1 hour is unsuitable).
Verify the pH of the fixative is 7.4 to ensure optimal staining.

steps.title: Label and seal samples
steps.instruction: Secure and label the samples for transport.

substeps.instruction: Label each tube with the animal number.
Parafilm each tube to minimize leaks.
Place tubes in a zip-lock bag.

steps.title: Prepare documentation and shipping
steps.instruction: Prepare a summary sheet and ship the samples according to the required timeline.

substeps.instruction: Create a summary sheet listing all animals, experimental description, date of death, and your name and email address.
If apoptosis is to be assessed, ensure eyes are received within approximately 4 days of death and fixation.
Provide a few days of warning before shipping and email the tracking number once sent.
